_about: Machine-readable field registry for Voice Agent v2 (Expert Mode). SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the field set and each field's `authoring` class. Human view: schema.md. Full authoring-class definitions: README.md#the-authoring-tiers-full-field-partition. If a field's class changes, change it HERE first. `resourceKind` appears only on reference/environment fields; `notes` reference schema.md section numbers. The top-level key `skills` has no `topLevel` row of its own: it is the container key for the whole `skills` section below, and the validator recognizes it from there.
_enabledRule: Every skill object present in the config, every scenario, and every guardrail MUST carry an explicit `enabled` bool. Nothing defaults it: a missing key fails the save with 422 (`expected required property enabled to be present`), and a stored unit without it is silently inactive. `enabled: false` is a legal shape -- it ships a unit switched-off for the user to finish in the dashboard.

authoringClasses.generate: Generator authors freely (content/choice/number). Self-contained: nothing outside the JSON is required.
authoringClasses.reference: Points to a company-scoped resource by ID. Never invent a real ID, guess one, or leave a placeholder: REUSE the real ID already on the agent (the Expert-Mode editor shows the current config) when it fits the use case, else use a zero-touch substitute where one exists, ask the user for the real ID and put it in, ship the skill switched off (transfers: enabled false + rules []), or omit the feature and tell the user to wire it in the UI (generator-contract.md reference decision tree).
authoringClasses.environment: Environment-specific phone-number selector. defaultOutboundNumberId defaults to 1 (Automatic), exactly as the dashboard seeds it -- never invent or copy a specific id from an example. Only 1 is magic (Automatic); every other value, INCLUDING 2, is a literal phone-number ID the company must own (there is no backend 'Random'), and an unowned id is a hard 400 with no self-heal. The save never auto-picks a number, so 1 needs a real owned failoverOutboundNumberId in BOTH directions to complete it -- there is no inbound carve-out, and null is never valid (omit the failover key only when defaultOutboundNumberId is a real non-1 id). Completing the failover is the FE-faithful path: reuse the values on the agent's pasted config, obtain them from cloudtalk_list_numbers when connected, or -- offline -- the user completes it in the dashboard. Setting a real owned defaultOutboundNumberId directly is the alternative; do not present a bare 1 with no failover, which will 400.
authoringClasses.forbidden: Never emit. Either computed/response-only, OR system-managed by the dashboard/BE (the Expert-Mode editor sets these on save and the BE defaults them on create); ignored, stripped, or overridden on import.

topLevel.notes: Required, != 0, and CANNOT be omitted (the editor rejects a missing value; no preserve-on-omit). Defaults to 1 (Automatic), exactly as the dashboard seeds it; setting a specific number instead means a REAL owned id. Only 1 is magic: Automatic. Every other value -- INCLUDING 2 -- is a literal phone-number ID the company must own; there is no backend 'Random' (2 only ever 'worked' if a company happened to own number id 2), and an id the company does not own is a hard 400 naming that number, with no self-heal. Connected: obtain a real id from cloudtalk_list_numbers, or reuse the id on the user's pasted config when editing. If you use Automatic (1), failoverOutboundNumberId MUST be a real owned id in BOTH directions to complete it -- the FE-faithful path. Never guess a value like 2; offline, the user completes the failover/number in the dashboard. Required even for inbound agents, which never call out.

The number Automatic (1) falls back to. Whenever defaultOutboundNumberId is 1 (Automatic) this is REQUIRED in BOTH directions -- there is no inbound carve-out -- and must be a real owned number id: the save 400s without it and nothing self-heals it. Carry the agent's real value when editing, or obtain one from cloudtalk_list_numbers. OMIT the key only when defaultOutboundNumberId is a real non-1 id; never emit null (unsupported, and identical to absent on import).
Must be in the resolved provider's supported set (schema 4.3, 5).
Presence forces ElevenLabs and marks the agent "complex" (schema 5). When set, also pin providerOverride: "elevenlabs".

Hard ceiling in MINUTES -- the call is cut off when reached. Required; the editor fills 30 if omitted, and there is no server default (no 240). There is NO hard API cap, but keep it to 120 or below (~20-30 min inbound, ~10-15 min outbound is typical); a ceiling above 120 draws a recommendation warning, not a save refusal. Set generous headroom above the expected length; tighten only for an intended hard stop (behavioral 4.4).
LLM sampling temperature. Baseline 0.5; highly structured/deterministic flows may go lower (~0.1-0.3) (behavioral 7a-bis).

A voice ID from the voice library. The four premade default voices (schema 4.4) are global, not company-scoped, and usable on BOTH providers (CloudTalk serves ElevenLabs voices for every provider), so picking from them is self-contained; there is no MCP/plugin tool to list voices, so use that documented set or reuse a voice from an existing agent. Default when unsure: cgSgspJ2msm6clMCkdW9 (Jessica, the only female in the default set). ALWAYS advise the user to pick their preferred voice in the dashboard voice picker, where the full language-filtered catalog lives.

NOT API-required: the API does not demand the key and applies no helpful default -- omitting it on a full-document write RESETS it to 0 instead of preserving it, so an omission is a silent behavior change, never a no-op. The value passes straight through to ElevenLabs. Baseline 2, never 4 (behavioral 7a-bis). Always emit it deliberately and carry the stored value forward on updates. Unlike elevenLabsSettings (omit-to-let-provider-default), this is not backfilled.

Voice stability, passed straight through to ElevenLabs untouched. REQUIRED and NOT backfilled -- the API applies no default, so omitting it fails the save. Baseline 0.3 (behavioral 7a-bis). Distinct from elevenLabsSettings knobs, which are omit-to-let-provider-default.
Voice similarity boost, passed straight through to ElevenLabs untouched. REQUIRED and NOT backfilled -- the API applies no default, so omitting it fails the save. Baseline 0.7 (behavioral 7a-bis).

Canonical model ID from the 25-model registry (schema 4.2, format "<vendor> - <model>", vendor in openai|anthropic|google|qwen); must be offered by the resolved provider (ElevenLabs offers all 25, Deepgram only 14) or the save 400s. The LLM is auto-selected server-side unless this is set (schema 5). Default recommendation: anthropic - claude-haiku-4-5 (valid on both providers).
Usually omitted (auto-selected). MUST be "elevenlabs" whenever secondaryLanguages is set — pins multilingual to ElevenLabs so a stored Deepgram provider can't reject the save (schema 5).

5-120 s, or 0 = provider default. Preserve-on-omit on a full-document update. Anything above 90 saves but is REJECTED when the call is dispatched -- the call is never placed -- so keep it at 90 or below.

ElevenLabs-only tuning (schema 10). Ignored on Deepgram agents. The API enforces the turnEagerness/turnModel enums AND backgroundSound.preset (required-when-present, 9-value enum) and backgroundSound.volume [0,1]; the remaining sub-field shapes are unchecked server-side, so they are validated in code. Unknown keys are rejected by /validate (nested included) but SILENTLY DROPPED by the save. Preserve-on-omit at the OBJECT level: omit it and the stored settings are kept; send it and it REPLACES them.

subFields.notes: Start composing the reply before the caller finishes; cuts perceived latency.
How readily the agent takes its turn. One of the two enums the API itself enforces.
Turn-detection model version. turn_v3 is safe through this API, which pins the ASR provider it needs.
Ignore background voices. A FLAG, not an object: the nested background_voice_detection shape is built server-side and is never accepted as input.
Non-empty strings; boosts recognition of niche words and product names.
Non-empty strings; caller acknowledgements that must not count as an interruption. Set together with interruptionIgnoreTermLanguages -- terms alone silently do nothing at runtime.
Non-empty strings; the languages the ignore-terms are matched in.
REQUIRED whenever the backgroundSound object is present. Omit the whole object to play no ambient bed.
Optional; loops the ambient bed seamlessly.

topLevel.notes: Response-length preset (schema 11): concise | standard | thorough. ""/omitted = unset, and an unset value self-heals to "standard" server-side. In connected mode the MCP write schema now carries this enum (the empty string included) and REJECTS anything else as invalid_args before the platform sees it; offline, the local validator is the gate. No enum key in this registry: the top-level enum check has no room for the legal empty string, so verbosity is validated in code.

Identity tone presets (schema 11), a fixed 6-label allowlist with no free text. Array field: the enum applies PER ELEMENT and is validated in code, so []/omitted still passes as unset. In connected mode the MCP write schema carries this allowlist too and rejects anything else as invalid_args. An unset value self-heals to ["friendly","direct"] server-side, and duplicate labels are deduped at save time (both create and update). Prefer one or two labels — a wider blend expresses each preset more weakly.

MUST be true when direction == inbound (BE-enforced). Gates `greeting` (agent speaks the greeting only when true). Author-supplied in Expert Mode and respected; the setup wizard derives it as !!greeting, but that is the wizard path, not Expert Mode. Generator: true whenever a greeting is emitted.
The agent's core behavioral instructions. Can be substantial -- a soft target of up to ~250 words (behavioral 2.1); only a genuinely empty or one-line prompt is flagged as thin.
Spoken verbatim as the first line (NOT auto-generated for v2). Empty -> inbound uses a runtime default, outbound stays silent. There is no `firstMessage` field.
Per-element; action sub-values change the class - see scenarioActions. Every element MUST carry an explicit `enabled` bool (schema 7.1).

ACCEPTED BUT INERT -- do not author; keep the array empty. The config API stores guardrails, but the runtime model has no `enabled` field, so at runtime they deserialize to enabled=false and are silently skipped -- they do not take effect until the API carries a runtime enabled field. Put always-on safety rules in the goalPrompt `## Guardrails` prose section instead (behavioral 2.1). The validator warns (guardrails-inert) on any non-empty array. Shape if ever populated: each element {enabled, when, reply}, all three required (schema 7.2).
IDs of ACTIVE knowledge bases the company owns. NO preserve-on-omit: on a full-document update an omitted key unlinks every KB, so carry the current value forward when editing an existing agent.

transferToHuman.notes: Required bool. When you don't have a complete real target, ship a DISABLED DRAFT (`enabled: false`): either scaffold the intended group (a rule with destination "group" and groupId/groupExtension OMITTED) or send `rules: []` when no group is in mind. Both save cleanly and the dashboard shows the skill as "Requires configuration" for the user to finish setting up the transfer to their team, then switch it on. Use `enabled: true` only with a complete real pair; an ENABLED skill needs at least one rule (empty rules on an enabled skill is save-refused).

REQUIRED as soon as the skill object exists -- an omitted key is rejected on import (422). Two draft shapes: [] (no group in mind, legal only while the skill is switched OFF) or a rule scaffolding destination "group" with the id/extension OMITTED (the default -- keeps the group intent visible). An ENABLED transferToHuman needs at least one rule. Every present rule needs the `condition` and `destination` keys.

Optional bool. The scaffold defaults it to true (the dashboard create-time default) -- the agent announces the handoff before transferring; leave it off only where speed beats the announcement, such as a pure routing or triage line (behavioral 3.4).

DEFAULT is a direct transfer, and a group is the preferred human target. On an ENABLED rule "agent"/"group" need BOTH halves of their pair (agentId + agentExtension / groupId + groupExtension): the API requires both, and NOTHING downstream validates the values -- the FE forwards them verbatim, the API has no ownership check, the runtime dials them raw -- so a wrong or half-set target on a live skill fails only mid-call. Where advanced transfer is enabled agent/group run attended (the caller stays with the AI while the second leg is placed, and a busy/declined/timed-out/dropped leg bounces back to the AI); where it is not they fall back to cold. On a SWITCHED-OFF draft OMIT the id/extension keys (agentId/groupId are integers -- an empty string is an INVALID_TYPE the save rejects even on a disabled skill; never blank them to "") -- the user completes the target in the dashboard; a group's extension can't be read programmatically, so a group draft with destination "group" and the ids omitted is the default way to scaffold a transfer. "call_flow" is generate (no ID: the agent hangs up and the flow continues -- always a cold hand-off) but is emitted ONLY when the user says the agent runs inside a Call Flow; for a standalone agent it is just a hangup. "" is the legal "not decided yet" destination value on a switched-off skill.

Integer id. On an enabled rule, emit together with agentExtension -- never guess either value. On a switched-off draft OMIT the key for the user to finish in the dashboard; never blank it to "" (an integer id rejects an empty string as an invalid type even on a disabled skill).
String extension. On a switched-off draft OMIT it rather than sending "".

Integer id. On an enabled rule, emit together with groupExtension -- never guess either value. On a switched-off draft OMIT the key (with groupExtension) to scaffold the group target for the user to complete in the dashboard (a group's extension can't be read programmatically); never blank it to "" (an integer id rejects an empty string as an invalid type even on a disabled skill). Prefer a group over a single agent: more targets can answer before an attended transfer falls back; a lone unavailable agent is a cold drop where advanced transfer is not enabled.
String extension. On a switched-off draft OMIT it rather than sending "".

The data extracted and handed to the human who picks up the transferred call, so they have context: callerName and/or summary. Not caller-facing. The scaffold default is [callerName, summary] (the dashboard create-time default).

Extra facts (same {name, type(UPPERCASE), description} shape as extractData properties) handed to the receiving human alongside includeProperties -- handover context for the person picking up the transfer, not a second data-capture schema.

extractData.notes: A LIST of {name, type(UPPERCASE), description}; type in STRING|NUMBER|BOOLEAN|ARRAY. PASSIVE and post-call: extraction runs after the call against the transcript, NOT during the conversation -- declaring a property does not make the agent ask for it. To actively collect a value, put the ask in goalPrompt (or a custom skill) AND declare the matching property (behavioral 3.1). Example lead-qual set: full name (STRING), company size (STRING/NUMBER), budget range (STRING), callback requested (BOOLEAN).
Optional webhook URL supplied by the user; not a company-resource ID.

answerQuestions.notes: 3-value enum. admitUncertainty / offerAlternative are self-contained (generate, no target). transferToHuman requires transferConfig (-> reference).

Same destination rules as transferToHuman.rules: destination is the fixed enum agent|group|call_flow, but the concrete target IDs are FREE-FORM (agent id+extension from list_agents; group id+extension) -- NOT an API-provided option list. Don't emit a wired group target here either (a group's extension can't be read programmatically): scaffold transferToHuman as a disabled draft (a rule with destination "group" and the id/extension OMITTED) for the user to finish in the dashboard, or -- simpler -- pick admitUncertainty/offerAlternative, which need no target.

appointmentBooking.notes: Required bool. `enabled: true` needs a real connected calendar integration (integrationId + calendarId, both reference); until those exist ship a DISABLED DRAFT (`enabled: false`) and the dashboard shows the skill as "Requires configuration" for the user to finish.
Any positive duration (e.g. 15 or 30 minutes); whatever the booked service needs.
A description of the service, made available to the voice-agent LLM so it knows what it is booking and can communicate it to the contact.
The description written onto the scheduled calendar event itself (may be customer-facing).

scenarioActions.notes: REQUIRED plain bool on every scenario: a missing key fails the save with 422 (`expected required property enabled to be present`), the API's own /validate endpoint does NOT catch it (the absent key decodes to disabled, so it only warns), and a stored scenario without it never fires. Same contract on every guardrail and on every skill object present in the config.

Optional; default "custom" when omitted. "custom" requires a non-empty `when`. "booking_confirmed" fires automatically after a successful in-call booking and may omit `when` (the API auto-fills it with "the booking is confirmed"); pair with action "sendSms" using {{appointment.*}} to text a booking confirmation. Any other value -> 422 (schema 7.1).

Self-contained. The ONLY way to give the agent the end_call ability -- and it must be EXPLICIT: an omitted action is a plain reply, not a hangup, and only an `enabled: true` hangup scenario grants end_call.
Requires toolReferenceId. FE strips this action on cross-company import.
Requires params.senderNumber (company-owned). FE strips; backend hard-rejects unowned numbers.

FIXED config text -- the LLM only decides whether to send, never writes/edits the body. Templated: {{...}} variables resolve (call-placement vars, {{caller_number}}, {{contact.*}}, {{appointment.*}} post-booking; behavioral 6). An unknown/unset variable resolves to an EMPTY STRING (silently deleted, no braces). NEVER invent a URL or a {{placeholder}}: URLs must be user-supplied verbatim, and there is no per-call/booking-link variable.

forbidden.reason: response-only diagnostic: recomputed server-side on every save, so a GET response round-trips safely into an update; authoring it has no effect
response-only diagnostics: the platform emits them alongside a read or a save to describe what it found. Never author them -- they are the server talking back, not config
response-only diagnostics: per-reference failure codes the platform attaches to a config (an unusable voice, an unowned number). A SUCCESSFUL save can carry them -- read them, never write them
FE export tag; API ignores; used only for cross-company import detection
does not exist in v2; the greeting field is `greeting`

System-managed: a real stored field (preserve-on-omit) that shelters the agent from future automatic provider/LLM/minorVersion upgrades, BUT the Expert-Mode editor force-sets it to true on save. It has no effect at creation, since new agents are stamped at the latest minorVersion. Generator omits it; the editor sets it.
